title: Greece TrainOSE sale and the Tempi crash
why: The 2015 bailout deal required binding-offer deadlines for TrainOSE (International Railway Journal), but no opened source ties the 2023 Tempi crash (57 dead) to the sale; the crash involved the state network's signalling and staffing. No other documented harm from the sale was found.

title: Lesotho Queen 'Mamohato hospital PPP
why: The IFC was paid adviser on the deal and Oxfam documents the hospital taking 51% of the health budget, but no loan condition or program requirement was found; advisory work does not meet the test.

title: Kenya–Uganda railway concession (Rift Valley Railways)
why: IFC arranged the deal and 4,200 workers were retrenched without pay-outs (IPS 2008), but no IMF or World Bank loan condition was found; only an MP's claim of donor pressure.

title: Mali EDM sale to SAUR
why: An IMF 1998 timetable required EDM's privatization, but the study opened (Estache and Grifell-Tatjé 2010) found water prices fell slightly and connections rose; no documented harm.

title: Pension privatizations (Kazakhstan, Hungary, Peru, Bolivia)
why: The ILO 2018 study says the World Bank and IMF backed most pension privatizations, but no country-specific loan condition could be opened before the search budget ran out.

title: Zambia Railways concession (RSZ)
why: Lusaka Times documents failures and the 2012 revocation, but the opened source does not describe any World Bank condition.

title: Mozambique 2010 bread riots

title: Cameroon February 2008 riots

title: Guinea 2007 general strike

title: Morocco 2014 fuel subsidy reform
